item.text: I’m taking a second pass to find structural issues that remain after the first cleanup, especially API inconsistencies and hidden correctness risks. Then I’ll refactor around a clearer core interface instead of just renaming things.

There’s still a real correctness gap: `decreaseKey` and `increaseKey` don’t enforce their contracts, so callers can silently corrupt heap order by passing the wrong direction. I’m refactoring around a clearer core API and then keeping the older method names as compatibility wrappers.

I’m editing the heap to centralize mutations in `offer` / `removeMin` / `removeAt` / `updateValue`, add explicit directional validation, and expand the test coverage around the new API and edge cases.
The first patch didn’t apply cleanly, so I’m rewriting the class in one pass to avoid a partial edit and keep the refactor coherent.
The second refactor is in place. I’m compiling and running the expanded tests now; if anything breaks, it’ll likely be in the new `removeAt`/directional-update paths.

Further refactored the heap around a clearer core API in [MinHeap.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/011_binary_heap/MinHeap.java:16). The main structural change is that mutations now flow through `offer`, `removeMin`, `removeAt`, and `updateValue`, while the older names like `insertKey`, `getMin`, `extractMin`, and `deleteKey` remain as compatibility wrappers. That removes the old sentinel-based delete path and makes the implementation easier to reason about.

I also fixed a correctness problem in the previous version: `decreaseKey` and `increaseKey` now enforce their contracts instead of silently accepting the wrong direction and risking heap corruption. That logic is in [MinHeap.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/011_binary_heap/MinHeap.java:95) and [MinHeap.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/011_binary_heap/MinHeap.java:167). Additional small API improvements include `isFull`, `capacity`, and `valueAt`.

The test harness in [MinHeapTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/011_binary_heap/MinHeapTest.java:4) now covers the newer queue-style API, direct indexed removal, directional validation, and empty-heap behavior in addition to the original example flow.

Verification: `javac MinHeap.java MinHeapTest.java && java MinHeapTest` passed.
